datasets.name: Landslide4Sense dataset
datasets.verbatim: In this study, we use the publicly available Landslide4Sense dataset (see Section 4.1.1 for details) to train both our proposed model and the comparison models.

datasets.name: Sentinel-2 images
datasets.verbatim: The Sentinel- 2 images are acquired and processed using Google Earth Engine (GEE).

datasets.name: Topographic information (slope and DEM data)
datasets.source: L-band synthetic aperture radar (PALSAR) launched by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency
datasets.verbatim: The topographic information is acquired by the L- band synthetic aperture radar (PALSAR) launched by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency with a spatial resolution of 12.5 m.

methods.name: MFDF-Net
methods.summary: An end-to-end landslide detection model based on differential fusion of multi-level features from optical remote sensing images and topographical data. It uses two ResNet-18 backbones to extract features, which are then fused using a spatial feature fusion module (SP-FFM) for low-level features and a semantic feature fusion module (SE-FFM) for high-level features, followed by a decoder with skip connections.
methods.verbatim: In response to these issues, we introduce topographic data based on optical remote sensing images and propose an innovative solution—an end- to- end new landslide detection model, MFDF- Net, which incorporates innovative feature fusion techniques.

availability.author_statement: The data that support the findings of this study are available from the corresponding author, upon reasonable request.

reproducibility_assessment: The landslide inventory and other input datasets are mentioned but not linked, and the custom code for the MFDF-Net model is not provided or linked.
